nina: Heads-up: hitting failures in a sample app when using the autogenerated pydantic models + AsyncClient under strict type checking. repro seems tied to `from __future__ import annotations` combined with pydantic v2 style models in stubs.

tom: can you paste the error? pyright or mypy?

nina: pyright (typeCheckingMode: strict) complains `Type of \"client.chat.stream\" is \"Any\"` and mypy gives `error: \"Coroutine\" not subscriptable` at call sites. minimal snippet: 
```py
from __future__ import annotations
from redwood import AsyncClient, models
client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.environ['API_KEY'])
async def main():
    async for ev in client.chat.stream("hi"):
        print(ev.type)
```

rahul: interesting — we recently switched stubgen to emit forward refs when annotations future is present which might interact poorly with how we import typing generics. do you have the generated .pyi?

nina: yeah attaching output gist in thread: https://gist.github.com/nina/repro-typing. key bit in pyi: `def stream(...) -> AsyncIterator: ...` instead of `AsyncIterator[models.ChatEvent]`. also several uses of `Annotated` without importing `typing_extensions.Annotated`.

marie: that sounds different from the usual missing-subscript bug. could be the resolver treating forward refs as strings and then failing to normalize during render. PR idea: when `from __future__ import annotations` detected in input schema, force-evaluate annotations to concrete types before pyi emit, or at least add proper typing imports and avoid bare generics.

tom: workaround for now: explicit cast in caller - `from typing import AsyncIterator, cast` then `it = cast(AsyncIterator[models.ChatEvent], client.chat.stream("hi"))`. ugly but works. also adding `# type: ignore[assignment]` at call site is another quick patch.

rahul: can you open an issue/PR with repro and note pydantic version? I suspect pydantic v2's use of Annotated is also in the mix.

nina: filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/1012 and pushed a tiny repro branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/4601 that adds a pyright/mypy smoke test against the generated stubs.

dev-bot: CI: stub-typing-smoke failed on py310: https://ci.redwood.dev/4601/3 — see log for missing imports (Annotated, AsyncIterator).

marie: I'll take the follow-up to make the pyi renderer ensure `from typing import AsyncIterator, Coroutine, Union` and `from typing_extensions import Annotated` are emitted when needed. add a unit that asserts no bare generics remain.

tom: also check if our packaging strips typing info when installed with `pip install -e .` using PEP 561 metadata; sometimes stubs get left out of wheel builds which causes installed users to see Any.

nina: thanks all. i'll update the issue with the exact error texts from both mypy/pyright and the reproducible install steps. saved us some hours. :coffee:
